bullets.title: NVDA: GPU resellers flood market post-BIS China remote-access restrictions; Jensen to testify Dec 1-3
bullets.body: Since the Nov 16 BIS interim final rule restricting Chinese remote access to advanced chips in third-party data centers, an unusually high number of NVIDIA GPUs have come to market from resellers — chips originally destined for data centers renting compute to Chinese firms. New license requirements also added for advanced semis to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Separately, Jensen Huang testifies before House committees Dec 1-2 and Senate Banking Dec 3 at a hearing titled 'Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of US Export Controls.'

bullets.title: DELL: Q3 blowout on AI server demand; management says demand still strengthening, not peaking
bullets.body: Dell's Q3 results beat on both AI and traditional server demand, with management commentary emphasizing demand is still strengthening rather than peaking — a bullish read-through for the AI compute capex theme broadly.

bullets.title: CRM: Wolfe cuts PT to $250 from $360 on softer field checks
bullets.body: Wolfe Research reduced its Salesforce price target to $250 from $360 after softer channel checks, noting organic revenue numbers 'feel too high.' The Wolfe All-SaaS index fell 7.31% week-over-week; SOX down ~10% over the past week despite Jensen Huang commentary.

bullets.title: PANW: Former regional VP files accounting fraud lawsuit alleging revenue misrepresentation
bullets.body: A former Palo Alto Networks regional VP filed a lawsuit accusing the company of accounting fraud, specifically alleging efforts to misrepresent deals as booked revenues to boost earnings. No company response cited.

bullets.title: ADSK: Q3 beat + FY27 guidance raise; KeyBanc reiterates OW at $341 PT on 12% organic growth + MaintainX upside
bullets.body: Autodesk beat Q3 EPS by 4.2% and raised FY27 billings guidance to ~11% y/y growth; MaintainX contributed $33M in F3Q vs. ~$28M expected. KeyBanc reiterates Overweight with $341 PT (23x FY28 EV/FCF), noting ADSK trades at 18x FY28 EV/FCF vs. industrial software peers at 23.5x. 85% of sell-side rated Buy; FY28 visibility clouded by FX and sales reorg lapping effects.

bullets.title: MDB: Narrative dominated by leadership transition and M&A speculation
bullets.body: Wolfe flagged that MongoDB's stock story is currently dominated by the CEO transition and M&A questions rather than fundamentals, with no specific guidance change noted.

bullets.title: SNOW: Checks solid; long-tilted view but risk-off market limits upside near-term
bullets.body: Wolfe's channel checks on Snowflake came in solid with a long-tilted view, but cautions that a risk-off market environment could cap near-term upside.

bullets.title: META: +3.4% on Muse AI-Walmart integration; AR/VR demand at ~16% holiday intent
bullets.body: Meta's Muse AI agent was integrated with Walmart's retail platform for Black Friday deal discovery, driving a 3.4% gain. Separately, Citi's holiday electronics survey shows ~16% of consumers intend to purchase AR/VR headsets/smart glasses, a positive read-through for Meta's wearables/Reality Labs business.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone captures 42% of holiday smartphone purchase intent; AI replacement cycle supportive
bullets.body: Citi's US holiday electronics survey ranks smartphones #1 at 51% purchase intent, with iPhone and Samsung Galaxy each at 42% share. MacBook Air/Pro tied with Windows desktops at ~24% for PC purchases. Results support AI-driven replacement activity thesis.

bullets.title: NFLX: Acquires Radford Studio Center for $380M; bidding for FIFA World Cup rights
bullets.body: Netflix purchased the 1.14M sq ft Radford Studio Center in LA for $380M — its first owned LA studio lot — and is reportedly bidding for FIFA World Cup broadcast rights. Stock gained ~0.9% on the news.

bullets.title: AFRM: +3.2% in fintech outperformance week; cards/payments group +4.0%
bullets.body: Affirm gained 3.2% as the cards/payments group outperformed the broader banking sector by ~6 points (group +4.0% vs. Investment Banks/Brokers -1.9%). PYPL +6.8% and FOUR +11.4% led the fintech cohort.

bullets.title: HOOD: -5.0% on the week; Wedbush initiates Outperform; stock gaining in sympathy with Bitcoin ~$60.1K
bullets.body: Robinhood fell 5% as Investment Banks/Brokers underperformed, but Wedbush initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and the stock is seeing sympathy moves with Bitcoin near $60,100.

bullets.title: UBER/TSLA: UBS forecasts $90bn US robotaxi market by 2040; both primary coverage names
bullets.body: UBS published a detailed Q-Series on the US robotaxi market sizing it at ~$90bn annual gross bookings by 2040 on ~600k robotaxis, with Tesla and Uber as the primary company focus areas; base, bull, and bear scenarios modeled.

bullets.title: TSLA: EV mix tracking modestly higher sequentially; RIVN R2 cited as credible competitive threat
bullets.body: JPM's November auto review notes BEV penetration tracking modestly above October's 6.3% mix. The Rivian R2 is flagged as an emerging credible competitive threat to Tesla in the mid-size SUV segment.

bullets.title: Semi positioning: 3z net selling over 20 days; UBS sees valuations pricing ~25-30% compute capacity cuts
bullets.body: JPM positioning data shows US Semis saw 3z net selling over 20 days with shorting at +4z level — a potential setup for a reversal if volatility recedes. UBS independently notes semis are now pricing in ~25-30% cuts to 2028 compute capacity, calling valuations 'attractive.' JPM sees AI stocks poised for Dec/Jan recovery post Oct/Nov capitulation.

bullets.title: WDAY: Q3 beat with AI ARR +130% y/y; raised FY27 guidance but FQ4 sub revenue/cRPO disappointed
bullets.body: Workday beat Q3 with AI ARR up 130% y/y and raised full-year guidance, but FQ4 subscription revenue and cRPO outlooks disappointed. The stock traded higher but Wolfe notes 11% next-year sub revenue growth target remains questionable.

bullets.title: OKTA: Positive checks with cRPO acceleration in F3Q and F4Q guide; AI momentum building
bullets.body: Wolfe's channel checks on Okta came in positive, showing cRPO acceleration in both F3Q actuals and F4Q guidance. AI momentum described as early but progressing.

bullets.title: CRWD/ZS: CRWD acquired ZS in largest-ever security deal; combined entity better positioned for AI security despite selloff
bullets.body: CrowdStrike acquired Zscaler in what Wolfe describes as the largest security deal in history. Despite a share price selloff post-announcement, Wolfe views the combined company as better positioned to gain AI security market share. CRWD reported impressive F3Q results alongside the deal.

bullets.title: TSM: JPM Asia OW; AI supercycle seen continuing with semis/hardware net income set to exceed $1tn by 2028
bullets.body: JPM's Asia 2027 outlook is bullish on the AI supercycle, with AI stocks comprising >50% of Asia index weight and expected to drive ~70% of earnings growth in 2027. TSMC is among the top 15 preferred stocks; JPM calls current bearish AI overbuilt-capex narrative 'stale.' Datacenter ROI >30% at current rental rates cited as evidence cycle is not peaking.

bullets.title: GLW: Lower TV spending modestly mixed; gaming/smartphone spend shift limits TV category growth
bullets.body: Citi's holiday survey shows TVs ranked below gaming peripherals (44% intent) and smartphones (51%) in purchase priority, creating a modest headwind for Corning's display glass business despite longer-term large-screen TV trends.
